coaching_points: Forechecker takes away useful ice instead of skating directly at the puck carrier.
Retriever protects the puck and uses changes of speed or direction to escape.
Progress from 1-on-1 to 2-on-2 or 3-on-3 once the angling habits are established.

title: NEHDA Loop N Drive - 4 Part Progression
description: A four-part progression built around a loop, exchange and net drive. Players move the puck quickly through support options, regroup back into the zone and finish with different deceptive shooting or escape techniques.
coaching_points: Communicate and present the stick as a target.
Keep the head up while transitioning around the net.
Time the return drive so the final pass arrives in stride.
Use each progression to change the shooting angle rather than repeating the same release.

title: Off The Wall - Neutral Zone Exchange
description: Two defensemen transition backward through the neutral zone, exchange the puck in front of each net, then finish with either a bank pass behind the net or a reverse before moving the puck back to the next player in line.
coaching_points: Prioritize pass quality and clear communication.
Maintain a consistent east-west gap between the defensemen.
On reverses, scan pressure before calling for the puck.

title: Double Regroup 2 on 1
description: Two forwards regroup twice with defensemen before turning the sequence into a 2-on-1. The drill runs continuously and can progress to a 3-on-1 or 3-on-2 by adding the trailing defenseman or another forward.
coaching_points: Forwards scan up ice before receiving the return pass.
Support with enough spacing to remain playable without stretching too far.
Defensemen protect middle ice and maintain gap through each regroup.

title: 2 on 1 Preds
description: The drill starts with a tight low 2-on-1. After the first scoring play, one forward tracks back to pressure the coach, the pair regains possession, uses the defenseman for a regroup and then attacks the original defender in a long 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Make the first low play quickly instead of overhandling.
Track hard immediately after the scoring chance.
Transition from the recovery into the regroup without stopping.
Defender recovers inside position before defending the long rush.

title: The Green Jump
description: Forwards exchange the puck with defensemen through the neutral zone. A D-to-D pass creates a new outlet, then both forwards and the original defenseman jump up ice together and fill lanes for a 3-on-0 attack.
coaching_points: Communicate before each exchange.
Keep sticks on the ice as clear passing targets.
Attack the regroup with pace and have all three players jump up ice together.

title: Bruins Neutral Zone
description: A multi-part neutral-zone flow drill. Players work D-to-D movement, post-and-bump support, wall chips and zone entries before progressing to an optional point shot with traffic.
coaching_points: Scan constantly because both sides are moving at the same time.
Communicate and present sticks as targets.
Keep support routes timed so bump passes arrive in stride.
On the final option, create a real screen or tip at the net.

title: Neutral Zone Chaos Drill
description: All ten skaters move randomly in the neutral zone until the coach starts live play by passing to either team. Both groups must instantly organize, with the offense attacking before structure forms and the defense recovering into position.
coaching_points: Everyone scans while moving before possession begins.
Offense attacks open space before the defense can fully organize.
Defense communicates immediately, protects middle ice and gets sticks into lanes.

title: Buffalo 2 on 1
description: Two forwards use a pair of defensemen to regroup through the neutral zone, build speed, and then attack one defender in a high-speed 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Communicate before receiving the puck.
Keep sticks available as passing targets.
Time the routes so both forwards arrive with speed and usable spacing.

title: Sens Regroup
description: The drill builds net-front pressure from 1-on-1 to 2-on-2 and 3-on-2, then transitions the same forwards and defensemen into a high-tempo neutral-zone regroup and 3-on-2 rush.
coaching_points: Create traffic and compete for positioning around the net.
Defensemen move laterally before shooting to change the lane.
Transition quickly on the final whistle and fill lanes for the 3-on-2.

title: 5 Player - Every Pass a One Touch
description: Five players regroup together in the neutral zone and attack up ice while every pass must be completed with one touch. A missed one-touch ends the repetition.
coaching_points: Scan before the puck arrives so the next play is already identified.
Communicate continuously and keep sticks on the ice.
Keep moving and maintain spacing through the regroup and entry.

title: Weak Side Transition
description: An offensive-zone shot and net-front battle immediately becomes a defensive reload, puck recovery, weak-side regroup and potential 2-on-1 back into the zone.
coaching_points: Reload from offense to defense immediately.
Close space and regain possession before transitioning back to attack.
Use weak-side speed and scan before receiving the transition pass.
Read whether the defender steps up or backs off into the 2-on-1.

title: NEHDA Defenseman Carousel
description: A continuous defense-focused passing sequence combining lateral point movement, an exchange behind the net, a breakout pass, point shot and slot activation.
coaching_points: Demand clean passing and clear communication.
Stay aware of all moving players before receiving the puck.
Time each route so the next option is ready without rushing the play.

title: 4 Corner Possession Game - Defensive Advantage
description: A 2-on-2 possession game with two stationary support players for each team positioned on its defensive side. Teams use corner support, give-and-go plays and quick puck movement around back-to-back nets.
coaching_points: Defenders keep sticks in lanes and angle attackers away from dangerous ice.
Attackers use support players and give-and-go movement instead of holding the puck.
Communicate constantly and scan around the reversed nets.

title: 32 Get Back
description: Three forwards track back to strip a puck carrier, move the recovered puck to the defensemen for a regroup, and then attack 3-on-0. A second puck creates another full-group reload and regroup before attacking again.
coaching_points: Track back through the puck carrier's hands and stick.
Move the recovered puck to support quickly.
Forwards keep heads up and spread into clear regroup options.
Attack through the middle before finishing the rush.

title: Regroup Game
description: A cross-ice 3-on-3 game where teams must regroup behind their own goal before attacking the opposite net. A center line can be added to require proper onside timing.
coaching_points: Offensive players work hard to become outlets and keep sticks available.
Defenders angle with sticks in passing lanes.
Communicate through every possession change and regroup.

title: Bernie Burner
description: A timing and rush-entry drill where a forward and defenseman exchange the puck, a second forward builds speed through the neutral zone, and the group enters with a delayed support route before creating a second scoring chance.
coaching_points: Prioritize timing over simply skating at maximum speed.
Keep sticks on the ice and communicate passing targets.
Enter with spacing so the secondary forward remains available.
After the first shot, recover the second puck quickly for the follow-up play.

title: Neutral Zone Regroup Drill
description: A five-player neutral-zone regroup progression that runs three different options: an immediate strong-side outlet, a D-to-D weak-side regroup, and a D-to-D hinge before attacking 3-on-0.
coaching_points: Forwards mirror the puck and maintain clear lane spacing through each regroup.
Defensemen identify the correct option early and move the puck without overhandling.
Center drives the net while the weak-side forward fills the high support lane.
Run all three variations so players learn reads instead of memorizing one route.

title: 3 Regroup 3 vs. 2 Drill
description: Three forwards regroup three times between two defense pairs, then attack the final pair in a 3-on-2. The drill emphasizes timing, lane spacing and quick puck movement through repeated regroups.
coaching_points: Forwards avoid getting ahead of the puck and fill separate lanes.
Defensemen scan up ice before moving the puck.
Keep the regroup passes crisp so the final 3-on-2 develops with speed.

title: Breakout Regroup Shooting
description: A continuous give-and-go breakout sequence. A player opens to the wall for a return pass, gives the puck back, then jumps into the slot for a quick one-timer before rotating to the goal line for the next repetition.
coaching_points: Present the stick as a target on the wall.
Communicate before receiving the return pass.
Keep the head up while moving into breakout position.
Release the shot quickly after the give-and-go.

title: 2 on 2 Continuous Transition
description: A continuous full-ice 2-on-2 transition drill. Two forwards attack two defensemen; when the play ends, a new pair of forwards and defensemen jump in and the puck immediately travels the other direction.
coaching_points: Defensemen hold a tight gap and communicate.
Forwards support the puck carrier and create a 2-on-1 when possible.
Transition immediately when possession or the rep ends.
Keep only one puck in play so the pace stays continuous.

title: 2 vs. 0 Rush Series #1
description: Two players exchange passes down one side, enter the zone with the outside player wide and the inside player driving the far post, then reverse direction for a second rush with transition skating and a wide shot.
coaching_points: Make multiple clean passes before the blue line.
Inside player drives the net with the stick available.
Outside player attacks wide before making the scoring play.
Keep the second rush moving with controlled transition skating.

title: 2 vs. 0 Rush Series #2
description: Two players pass up ice, then the outside player uses an escape around a tire to attack the slot while the inside player drives the net. On the return trip they use drop passes before creating a second scoring chance.
coaching_points: Outside player sells the wide route before cutting inside.
Net driver gets to the crease with timing and purpose.
Use controlled drop passes on the return rush.
Finish with a quick release from the high slot.

title: 2 vs. 0 Rush Series #3
description: Two players pass up ice, then the outside player cuts toward the middle and drops the puck to the inside player. The inside player takes the puck wide around the tire and returns it to the high slot for a quick shot, then the pair repeats the concept in the opposite direction.
coaching_points: Time the middle cut and drop pass so both players maintain speed.
Outside support stays available high in the slot.
Shoot quickly off the return pass.
Keep the route continuous and game-paced.

title: Quick Turn Up 1 on 1
description: A forward retrieves a puck near the red line, turns up ice around a marker and attacks a defender 1-on-1. The defender transitions into gap control and works to keep the rush outside.
coaching_points: Forward attacks with speed and reads available inside or outside ice.
Defender closes gap early and keeps the stick in a useful lane.
Use changes of pace and direction to create separation.

title: Quick Turn Up 2 on 1
description: Two forwards accelerate from center ice to a loose puck and immediately attack a defender 2-on-1. The setup recreates a neutral-zone turnover that turns into a quick scoring chance.
coaching_points: Puck carrier attacks decisively instead of slowing the rush.
Support forward gets open or drives the net.
Use deception and changes of pace to move the defender.
Defender keeps the stick in the passing lane and maintains a tight gap.

title: Quick Turn Up 2 On 2
description: Two forwards cross to build speed and attack two defensemen in a high-tempo 2-on-2 transition. The rep continues until the play is dead or the defense exits the zone.
coaching_points: Forwards generate speed before entering the attack.
Support away from the puck and use crossing or pace changes to create space.
Defenders communicate, hold a tight gap and steer the rush outside.

title: Speed 2 on 1
description: A high-tempo regroup drill that turns into a fast 2-on-1. The defenseman receives a pass while skating backward, transitions up ice and moves the puck to either forward. The forwards use a second regroup before attacking the original defender 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Forwards time middle and wide support so the defenseman has short passing options.
Attack the final 2-on-1 with speed and staggered lanes.
Defender protects the middle and keeps the stick in the passing lane.

title: 3 v 3 with 3 Ways to Score
description: A 3-on-3 game with three scoring methods: complete a pass through two defenders, complete a one-touch pass, or score a goal. Teams keep score throughout the game.
coaching_points: Defenders keep sticks in passing lanes and angle attackers outside.
Offense moves without the puck to create passing lanes.
Look for one-touch opportunities instead of holding the puck.

title: 3 Man Shooting Warm-Up
description: Three-player full-ice warm-up. The first player attacks for a shot, curls behind the net for a coach pass, then connects with the second player in the middle. The puck moves to the third player on the far side for the final shot while the first two drive for rebounds.
coaching_points: Communicate and present the stick as a target.
Time each route so nobody gets too far ahead or behind the puck.
Drive the net after moving the puck and look for rebounds.

title: 3 v 3 Neutral Zone Break Game
description: A competitive 3-on-3 neutral-zone game with goals on the blue lines. A team can send the puck behind its own blue line to activate a fresh pass from its coach, creating quick transition and fast-break opportunities.
coaching_points: Be ready for immediate transition when a new puck is activated.
Offensive players keep sticks available and jump into open ice.
Defenders scan all three attackers and keep sticks in passing lanes.

title: Duck Shooting
description: Forwards and defensemen work a continuous passing and shooting sequence. The defenseman receives and returns pucks in transition, forwards attack for shots and tips, and the final puck moves low-to-high for a point shot with traffic.
coaching_points: Communicate and keep sticks available on every exchange.
Time the skating routes so passes arrive in stride.
Net-front players screen the goalie and work for deflections.
Defenseman walks the line before the final shot.

title: Neutral Zone Puck Races With Support
description: Two players race for a loose puck in the neutral zone. Winning possession activates support and a weak-side option, while the losing side becomes the defense. The possession team must escape pressure and connect through support before entering the zone.
coaching_points: Use body position to win the puck race.
Escape pressure with tight turns and deception before passing.
Support players communicate loudly and become immediate outlets.

title: L-Support - Basic Triangle Movement
description: Three players continuously move and pass while maintaining an L-shaped support structure, with the puck carrier positioned at the elbow and the two off-puck players flanking as passing options.
coaching_points: Keep the puck at the elbow of the support shape.
Off-puck players flank the puck carrier instead of standing directly behind the play.
Treat the L as a flexible framework rather than a rigid geometric pattern.
Progress by adding one or two defenders.

title: 1 on 1 Re-Gap Transition
description: Defenders skate backward through the neutral zone, react to a whistle by transitioning forward, and re-gap against an attacker from the opposite side. The goal is to close space and force a turnover before the defensive blue line.
coaching_points: React immediately from backward to forward skating.
Close space before the blue line instead of backing in.
Establish stick-on-puck pressure before using the body.
Adjust the gap to the attacker's speed and depth.

title: NZ Regroup
description: Three forwards work through a neutral-zone regroup with defensemen before attacking up ice. The progression uses a second regroup option and can add a tracking player to create a four-player attack against two defenders.
coaching_points: Forwards time their routes so they stay underneath the puck and available.
Defensemen move the puck quickly D-to-D before finding the best outlet.
Attack the final rush with width, middle support and speed.

title: 2 on 2 Transition & Track
description: A continuous 2-on-2 transition game through the middle of the ice. New attackers activate as the puck changes direction while previous attackers track back and become part of the defensive pressure.
coaching_points: Transition immediately when possession changes.
Track through the middle and identify the most dangerous attacker.
Offense supports the puck with staggered lanes rather than skating side-by-side.

title: Side Middle Side
description: A whole-team passing warm-up with players stationed on both sides of the neutral zone. Pucks move side-to-middle-to-side while players exchange lanes and keep their heads up in traffic.
coaching_points: Scan before receiving because multiple pucks and players are moving at once.
Present a clear target and make firm passes.
Move immediately after passing instead of watching the puck.

title: 3 on 3 Transition Game
description: A continuous 3-on-3 game in one zone. Three attackers try to score while three defenders work to win possession and pass to the next group waiting outside the play, which immediately activates the next transition.
coaching_points: Attack quickly after transition instead of allowing the defense to reset.
Look for quick shots, tips and net drives.
Defenders support each other and move the puck cleanly to the next attacking group.

title: 2 v 2 Play Fast with Support
description: A high-tempo 2-on-2 game through center ice with two stationary support players in each team's offensive end. Players can use support for quick one- or two-touch passes and shots before immediately transitioning the other direction.
coaching_points: Use support early and sprint to become the next outlet.
Support players scan before the puck arrives so they can play quickly.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and force play away from middle ice.

title: 2 v 2 Shawzy
description: A coach randomly activates one of four lines to start a 2-on-2. The receiving team immediately attacks while the other side must step up, surf and angle the rush to the outside.
coaching_points: All four players stay ready to instantly become offense or defense.
Defenders step up and angle instead of retreating backward.
Forwards support each other and chip pucks into soft areas when pressure closes.

title: Drop Down 4 on 2
description: A defenseman starts the attack while three forwards drop into different neutral-zone support routes. The four-player unit organizes into a line rush against two defenders, then the opposite team retrieves a new puck and attacks back the other direction.
coaching_points: Mix low support, stretches and middle cuts instead of running one fixed route.
Maintain speed and spacing through the neutral zone.
Fill wide, kick-out and middle support roles naturally as players interchange.

title: Continuous 2 on 2 with Ozone D Options
description: A continuous 2-on-2 rush becomes a 4-on-2 offensive-zone situation when the attacking team's defensemen activate at the blue line. A turnover triggers the waiting forwards to attack back the other direction against the opposite defense.
coaching_points: Get the puck deep on the rush rather than turning it over high.
Defenders maintain strong gap on the initial 2-on-2.
Use the point options to create traffic, tips and side-lane plays.
On possession change, transition immediately into the counterattack.

title: 3 v 2 to 5 v 5 Backcheck
description: The drill starts with a live 3-on-2 down low. A second puck then triggers a 3-on-2 rush the other direction while the original five players backcheck and join, turning the play into full 5-on-5 in the far zone.
coaching_points: Backcheck through middle ice in straight lines.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and force the rush outside.
Offense supports the puck and enters with structure.
Finish by sorting full 5-on-5 defensive-zone coverage.

title: Short to Long 2 on 2
description: The same defense pair plays two consecutive 2-on-2 rushes: first a short rush from the near blue line, then a long regrouped rush from the opposite side. The progression forces defenders to reset their gap quickly while forwards attack with changing routes.
coaching_points: Forwards avoid straight-line attacks and use route changes to create confusion.
Defenders close a tight gap and angle the rush outside.
Reset quickly between the short and long 2-on-2.

title: 1 v 1 v 1 Game
description: Three players compete for one puck in a confined area. The puck carrier must protect possession against two opponents while scanning multiple threats. A gate variation awards points for carrying the puck through a central cone gate.
coaching_points: Stay toward middle ice when possible to preserve more escape options.
Use deception, tight turns and changes of speed to protect possession.
Keep the head up because pressure can come from two players.

title: Rim to Regroup 2v1 Drill
description: The first phase is a rim retrieval battle below the goal line that creates a quick slot shot. The players then transition up ice, recover a coach's puck near the red line, regroup and attack the same defender 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Compete for the rim and move the puck to the slot quickly.
Forwards accelerate out of the zone and communicate through the regroup.
Defender times the gap and protects the middle on the 2-on-1.

title: 2 v 2 Net Front Corner Battles with Support
description: A competitive 2-on-2 game with nets in the corners and two support players at the points for each team. Players battle for possession, use rims or board passes to the point, then work for shots, tips and redirects around the net.
coaching_points: Win body position before trying to make the next play.
Use the boards and point support instead of forcing pucks through traffic.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and box out at the net front.

title: 2 v 2 High Roll
description: One forward rims a puck to a teammate down low, who retrieves under pressure. The two attackers work against two defenders and use switches or high rolls to create separation and a scoring lane.
coaching_points: Retrieve cleanly and get off the wall quickly.
Supporting forward stays close enough to help while finding an open lane.
Use the high roll to separate from coverage and create a shooting window.

title: Sabre Half-line Keep Away
description: Two teams of three play keep-away across a dividing line. The team in possession can use all three players on its side, while only two opponents may cross the line to defend, creating repeated 3-on-2 possession situations.
coaching_points: Defenders pressure aggressively with stick-on-puck and active feet.
Offense keeps heads up and moves to create passing lanes.
Maintain one player on the possession side as support instead of all three chasing the puck.

title: Angle Add-On Game
description: A small-area angling game that starts as a 1-on-1 or 2-on-2. Defenders skate through assigned circles before closing on the rush, and the coach can activate additional players as the rep continues.
coaching_points: Take an inside-out angle and steer attackers toward lower-risk ice.
Match speed before closing rather than charging at the puck carrier.
Activated players join immediately as support or back pressure.

title: UAA Angle Station
description: A bumper creates a loose puck for an attacker while a defender commits to one side. The attacker must read the pressure and escape the opposite direction before the play becomes a live 1-on-1 to the net.
coaching_points: Attacker reads the defender's commitment and reacts immediately.
Defender uses footwork and stick position to steer the attack.
Compete through the whistle and rotate offense to defense.

title: Chaos to Shot Warm-up Drill
description: Players stickhandle with individual pucks through crowded neutral-zone traffic while coaches add pressure. On the second whistle they exit through different lanes and finish with shots from three different routes.
coaching_points: Keep the head and eyes up while handling in traffic.
React to pressure instead of following a memorized route.
Exit the chaos area with speed and get the shot off quickly.

title: Mirror Angling
description: Forward and defender mirror through cone routes before transitioning into a live 1-on-1. The forward works to protect the puck and drive the net while the defender matches speed and angles the attack outside.
coaching_points: Forward protects the puck through the defender's hands and attacks inside position.
Defender matches speed, keeps toe caps up ice and uses stick-on-puck pressure.
Defend skating forward rather than continually backing in.

title: Sparta Agility Skating & Passing Progression
description: A three-part progression in a tight obstacle area: first skate without pucks, then skate with individual pucks and finish with shots, then use one puck among three players while continuously moving and passing before attacking the net.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and scan through traffic.
Use deception and puck protection around obstacles.
Create passing lanes and support the puck continuously.
Keep moving through exchanges and switches.

title: ROC (Retrieval-Outlet-Continuous) Drill
description: A continuous retrieval-and-outlet flow. A player shoots, retrieves a corner puck with a cutback, finds wall support, then the support player moves the puck to the next player and re-enters the zone for a quick shot.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before every retrieval.
Use deception on the wall before escaping pressure.
Time support so the outlet is available at the right moment.
Catch and release quickly on the final shot.

title: Oswego Facing the Puck Passing Drill
description: A give-and-go passing drill built around always facing the puck. The player attacks one tire, exchanges a pass, transitions backward while staying open to the puck, then catches and shoots before repeating in the opposite direction.
coaching_points: Never turn the back to the puck.
Transition backward while staying ready to receive.
Communicate and present the stick as a target.
Catch and shoot with control after the transition.

title: Up Wall Exchange
description: A three-player passing flow along the wall. Players exchange passes while one skates backward, rotate through the middle and net-side support, then finish with a quick catch-and-release shot.
coaching_points: Maintain spacing and communicate through each exchange.
Open up facing the puck instead of turning away from the play.
Move the puck off the hip quickly and get the eyes up.
Shoot immediately after receiving the final pass.

title: Elmira Transition Retrieval Drill
description: A defense-focused retrieval progression. The player transitions backward, opens back to forward speed, retrieves three separate pucks and moves each puck to support players positioned on the hashmarks.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before every retrieval.
Use deceptive toes before committing to the pickup.
Escape both inside and toward the wall.
Keep eyes up and communicate on every outlet.

title: Oswego Double Retrieval Drill
description: A two-retrieval sequence. The player first retrieves and escapes a corner puck, then circles for a second retrieval, carries behind the net, makes the outlet to the blue line and finishes by screening or redirecting the point shot.
coaching_points: Use shoulder checks before both retrievals.
Sell deception with the feet before escaping.
Face up ice behind the net before making the outlet.
Finish the rep with real net-front presence.

title: Merrimack Deception Retrieval Drill
description: A continuous corner retrieval drill with passive forecheck pressure. The retriever sells one direction with the feet, escapes the other way, protects the puck and moves it back to the line before becoming the next pressure player.
coaching_points: Make the foot deception obvious enough to move the forechecker.
Protect the puck immediately after the pickup.
Stay quick and decisive under passive pressure.
Build the drill toward more realistic pressure as players improve.

title: Canisius D Retrieval Options
description: A multi-option defense retrieval progression using different pressure cues. The defenseman works net-side escapes, wall-side pressure, an overspeed route behind the net and a rim pickup before moving pucks to outlets or finishing with a quick shot.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before every retrieval.
Use feet and body position to sell deception.
Read whether pressure is arriving net-side or wall-side.
Make the outlet quickly once separation is created.

title: Kings Defense Retrieval
description: A three-part defense retrieval progression in a compact space. Defensemen work an individual outlet, partner support behind the net and a switch-style exchange before moving the puck up ice for quick shots.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before each pickup.
Use deception before entering the wall.
Mirror the partner to provide support on the opposite side.
Move the puck quickly after gaining control.

title: 2vs2 Crossroad Passing
description: A confined 2-on-2 puck-support game with two stationary support players on opposite sides. The team in possession works to move the puck from one outside support player to the other using movement and quick exchanges through the middle.
coaching_points: Move constantly to create passing options.
Use body position and deception to protect possession.
Find soft ice away from defenders.
Transition immediately after a turnover.

title: Pass and Move Circle
description: Players form a large circle and continuously pass and move. The receiver skates on the first touch, exchanges a quick one-touch give-and-go with a teammate, then moves the puck to a new target. Additional pucks can be added to raise the tempo.
coaching_points: Skate immediately on the first touch.
Use clean one-touch passes.
Keep the head up and communicate.
Read teammates before choosing the next target.

title: 3 x Wall Pick Ups with Shot Around Circle
description: The player jumps to the boards to collect a chipped puck and immediately moves it to support. The pickup-and-pass sequence repeats three times around the circle, with the third puck finishing as a shot on net.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before collecting each wall puck.
Get the puck off the wall cleanly before making the pass.
Stay balanced through each pickup.
Progress to different pickup and shooting techniques.

title: Quick Start Continuous Outlet
description: A continuous breakout-outlet progression. Players first work clean outlet passing, then add a board retrieval, then add a protected reverse curl before finding the outlet.
coaching_points: Make passing quality and communication the priority.
Use a quick start that keeps the ice in front of the defenseman.
Avoid unnecessarily turning the shoulders away from the play.
Pivot into a ready receiving position whenever possible.

title: D Double Up
description: A two-part full-ice breakout and transition progression. Defensemen retrieve under pressure with partner support, move the puck through forward outlets, then activate through the neutral zone and join an offensive-zone finish.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check and scan before the retrieval.
Partner defenseman stays tight and supports the middle.
Forwards time low and strong-side outlet routes.
Defensemen activate with purpose after moving the puck.

title: Gain Inside Position Progression
description: A three-step battle progression focused on winning inside body position. Players first race for a spotted puck, then add a bumper for a quick scoring play, then battle through controlled body contact before retrieving and attacking.
coaching_points: Win inside body position before reaching for the puck.
Use both stick and body to protect possession.
Communicate with the bumper on the second progression.
Battle through contact while maintaining balance and control.

title: Yellow Attack Timing - V1
description: A two-player timing drill built around a corner retrieval. One player chips a puck into the corner, the retriever shoulder-checks and brings it off the wall, then finds the first player timing a route to the slot or around the net for a quick shot.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before the retrieval and come off the wall with the head up.
Time the slot or net route so the passing lane opens naturally.
Communicate and use deception to create extra time and space.

title: Strip Transitions V1 & V2
description: A continuous strip-and-transition drill along the wall. One player strips the puck from a teammate, quickly transitions off the boards and finds another player timing a jump into the zone for a shot. The second progression changes the strip technique from a stick lift to knocking the puck off the boards.
coaching_points: Angle with the stick on the ice before going stick-on-puck.
Transition immediately after winning the puck and get the head up.
The receiving player times the jump and presents a clear target.
Use both strip techniques so players learn more than one way to recover possession.

title: Good Stick 2 v 2 or 3 v 3
description: A cross-ice 2-on-2 or 3-on-3 game where one team is restricted to using one hand on the stick. The constraint reinforces stick-led defending, positioning, body protection and quick support decisions under pressure.
coaching_points: Defenders lead with the stick and close passing lanes.
Use positioning and body angle instead of reaching.
Offensive players support closely and protect the puck with the body.
Move the puck quickly when the one-hand restriction limits control.

title: 3 Shot Off The Wall
description: A continuous three-shot sequence off the wall. The player comes off the boards for the first quick shot, uses a give-and-go for a second shot or one-timer, then drives the net for a third catch-and-release chance before passing to the next player.
coaching_points: Communicate and call for the puck.
Keep the stick on the ice as a clear target.
Release each shot quickly instead of overhandling.
Stay facing the puck through the entire sequence.

title: Mid Pair Wall Retrievals
description: Partners continuously chip pucks to the wall, retrieve them and pass back to each other. The progression emphasizes fake-forehand reverse curls, head-up quick passes and additional deceptive retrieval variations.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before every retrieval.
Keep the head up after controlling the puck.
Use toes, hips, stick, head and eyes to sell deception.
Move the puck cleanly back to the partner.

title: Quick Touch Passing & Shooting
description: A quick-touch passing and shooting sequence around the circle. Players exchange several short passes, open up around the circle, move the puck to the next player in line, then cut to the slot for a quick return pass and shot.
coaching_points: Communicate and make crisp passes.
Keep sticks on the ice and ready to receive.
Open the body to the puck while moving around the circle.
Shoot immediately off the final pass.

title: 4 v 2 Continuous Zone Entry
category: 4 on 2 / Zone Entry / Small Area Game
description: Four attackers enter against two defenders and try to score quickly off the rush. If the defense wins possession and moves the puck to waiting teammates, the next group immediately attacks while two previous attackers stay to defend.
coaching_points: Attack quickly before the defenders can organize.
Use a net driver and weak-side scoring option.
Defenders protect middle ice and keep sticks in passing lanes.
Transition immediately when possession changes.

title: Yellow Runner Rally
description: Three attackers battle two defenders after a contested rim retrieval. Once the offense wins possession, they build a three-player possession triangle with a climbing player, soft-ice support near the dot, and net-front presence.
coaching_points: First attacker secures the rim with body position and scans before the next touch.
Second attacker supports the battle while the third becomes a clear outlet.
After possession is won, spread into three distinct support roles instead of staying clustered.

title: 3 v 3 with Down Low Passer
category: 3 on 3 / Small Area Game / Net Front
description: Three-on-three net-front game with an unpressured passer behind the net. Offensive players work to get open in scoring areas while defenders play tight coverage in front and deny passing lanes.
coaching_points: Offensive players separate from coverage and present sticks as targets.
Defenders maintain inside position and keep sticks in passing lanes.
Use the passer behind the net to force defenders to scan and communicate.

title: False Start Drill: Goalie Tracking
description: Goalie tracking drill that teaches the eyes and head to lead movement before the body reacts. The goalie begins slightly off angle while the shooter waits for an early lower-body move, then releases the puck. Progressions add butterfly recovery and stay-down movement.
coaching_points: Lead every movement with the eyes and head.
Track the puck all the way into the body or hands.
Bring the shoulders around with the head so the body arrives square.

title: Half Ice Finnish Skills Series with one Net
category: Half Ice / Puck Control / Passing / Shooting
description: Half-ice Finnish skills setup that adds a pass to start each repetition and a shot to finish. Players move through the skill pattern while staying spaced in two lines, then attack the net after completing the sequence.
coaching_points: Present a clear passing target before entering the skill pattern.
Keep the puck controlled while moving through the obstacles.
Finish the repetition with pace and a purposeful shot.

title: Half Ice Side By Side Skills Series #1
description: Side-by-side half-ice skills series built around control turns, backward puck control, inside-out circles and forward-facing transition work. The setup lets two lines work simultaneously for high repetition volume.
coaching_points: Lead turns with the head and upper body.
Use strong edges and a closed blade to keep puck control through turns.
Stay balanced through forward-to-backward and backward-to-forward transitions.

title: Footwork Shots #3
description: Advanced puck-control and shooting station using a tight obstacle pattern near the net. Players work quick feet and hands through the traffic before exiting into a shot.
coaching_points: Keep the feet active while handling through the obstacles.
Protect the puck from each obstacle instead of reaching around it.
Exit the pattern under control and finish quickly.

title: Circle Stickhandling Series
description: Three-part circle stickhandling progression. Players begin with creative puck control through obstacles, progress to following a moving partner while handling, then add passes to teammates positioned outside the circle.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and stay aware of other players in the circle.
Maintain full puck control while reacting to changing direction.
In the passing progression, identify the open target before moving the puck.

title: Continuous Warm Up Skills Series #1
description: Continuous full-ice warm-up that starts with partners passing in stride down the middle. At the far end both players turn outside, return in the outside lanes and work individual puck skills before rotating to the opposite line.
coaching_points: Receive and move the puck in stride.
Use a clean pass after one controlled stickhandle.
Keep the return route moving so the drill stays continuous with minimal waiting.

title: Continuous Warm Up Skills Series #2
description: Second continuous warm-up variation. Partners pass in stride down the ice, then turn outside with pucks and work a forward-backward transition pattern around cones before accelerating out and switching lines.
coaching_points: Make the pass in stride after one controlled touch.
Accelerate immediately out of every transition.
Switch lines so players repeat the passing pattern on both forehand and backhand sides.

title: Puck Protection Skill Drill
description: Player attacks a coach from the neutral-zone dot, receives a puck, sells an outside move, cuts inside and curls through pressure before attacking the slot for a shot. The coach stays connected throughout so the player has to keep the puck shielded while skating.
coaching_points: Keep the puck on the protected side of the body.
Use body position and skating speed instead of extra stickhandles.
Finish the final curl with the puck under control and attack the slot.

title: 2 on 0 Race for Puck
description: Two players pass while skating the length of the ice, finish the first rush at the net, then react to a second puck played into the neutral zone. The player who wins the race attacks while the other immediately becomes the defender for a 1-on-1.
coaching_points: Make multiple controlled passes on the initial 2-on-0 instead of rushing the sequence.
Drive the inside lane hard with the stick available for a pass.
On the second puck, transition immediately into attack or defensive angle based on who wins possession.

title: Corner Cycle Continuous Give & Go
description: Two-player cycle station. The first player retrieves a puck on the wall and cycles it down for the supporting player, then moves to the front of the net. The support player returns a pass for a quick shot and becomes the next retriever as the drill continues.
coaching_points: Communicate on both the cycle and the return pass.
Use the wall so the cycle puck arrives cleanly for the supporting player.
Open the blade and shoot immediately off the return pass when possible.

title: 1 v 1, 2 v 2, 3 v 3
category: 1 vs 1 / 2 vs 2 / 3 vs 3 Small Area Game
description: Cross-ice small-area game that grows from 1-on-1 to 2-on-2 to 3-on-3, then works back down as players rotate out on successive whistles.
coaching_points: Know who is entering and leaving on every whistle.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and angle to the outside.
Attackers move the puck quickly and look for fast shots.

title: 3 v 3 Pass to Coach
description: Three-on-three possession game where all three teammates must touch the puck before the group can pass back to the coach for a point.
coaching_points: Players without the puck win space and become passing options.
Support the puck carrier in tight areas.
React immediately after turnovers to regain possession.

title: 2 v 1 Keep Away
description: Two attackers play keep-away against one defender inside a circle, counting completed passes while the defender works to steal and protect possession.
coaching_points: Off-puck players move to open ice with sticks ready.
Puck carrier uses deception and protection to create lanes.
Defender stays between the two attackers with an active stick.

title: Sabre Half-Ice 2v2 With Outlets
description: Half-ice 2-on-2 game with outlet players available along the goal line and blue line. Players can use the outlets to create offense and extend possession.
coaching_points: Pass hard and quickly to outlet targets.
Keep eyes up and communicate before the puck arrives.
After using an outlet, move immediately to open ice for support.

title: 1 v 1 Race to Puck to 2 v 2
description: Two players race for a puck at center. The winner finds a teammate to create a 2-on-1 rush while the losing side backchecks, turning the play into a 2-on-2.
coaching_points: Win body position before reaching for the race puck.
Dot players anticipate whether they are joining offense or backchecking.
Transition immediately once possession is established.

title: Use the Nets Puck Protection
description: Defenseman retrieves behind a net while a forechecker applies pressure. Two closely spaced nets create a shield the puck carrier can use to escape pressure and find a breakout option.
coaching_points: Use the net as protection instead of exposing the puck.
Sell escapes with head, shoulders and stick position.
Stay patient until the passing lane is available.

title: Power Play Game Long Short
category: Power Play / 5 vs 3 / Small Area Game
description: Two power-play groups work on opposite halves of the zone. A coach starts one side with a rim; when the penalty killers clear it, the puck transfers to the other side and the next group attacks.
coaching_points: Make quick decisions in condensed space.
Use crisp puck movement to maintain possession.
Penalty killers clear decisively and protect the middle.

title: Power Play Face-Off Loss Drill
description: Power-play unit starts from a lost faceoff scenario and must retrieve a spotted puck before the penalty kill can clear, then create a shot quickly.
coaching_points: Win inside body position on retrievals.
Move the puck immediately after possession is recovered.
Generate the first shot within a few passes.

title: The D Initiate
description: Defenseman initiates the rush with a quick cross-ice pass, joins the attack as a late option, and receives a return pass for the final shot.
coaching_points: Sticks stay on the ice and ready for passes.
Defenseman pushes the pace and joins the rush.
Forwards gain middle ice and support underneath.

title: Half Ice Finnish Series Setup
description: Half-ice Finnish skill-development setup that can be reused for many variations, including mohawk pivots, backward underhandling, escapes and long-reach puck control.
coaching_points: Keep hips and shoulders controlled through pivots.
Cradle the puck smoothly while skating backward.
Use full reach and strong edges around every obstacle.

title: 2 v 1 Net Play Drills for Defensemen
description: Three-location 2-on-1 net-front series where forwards attack from behind the net or corners while one defender protects the slot and manages both threats.
coaching_points: Defender keeps the stick in passing lanes and scans both attackers.
Stay in a strong stance and protect the middle first.
Forwards attack the net and separate into open scoring space.

title: DZ Corner Battle 1 v 2 to 2 v 3
description: Defensive-zone battle progression that starts with one attacker against two defenders, then builds to two attackers against three defenders to train support, communication and coverage.
coaching_points: First defender pressures while the second supports.
Defenders communicate before switching pressure.
Attackers protect the puck and use support to create a scoring chance.

title: Pass Through 2 Players out of the Corner
description: Corner passing sequence where the puck carrier curls up the wall, gives the puck to the next player, then jumps into the slot to receive a return pass through two stationary defenders.
coaching_points: Jump into open ice with the stick presented.
Lead the moving player with the return pass.
Progress from passive to active sticks as execution improves.

title: D-Zone Coverage Tire Drill
description: Five-on-five defensive-zone coverage drill with a second phase where all three defending forwards skate around tires in the neutral zone before racing back to re-establish coverage.
coaching_points: Defenders keep sticks in lanes and sort coverage verbally.
Protect the middle while the forwards recover back into the zone.
Offense moves to open space while defenders are temporarily out of structure.

title: Outlet Game
description: Cross-ice game where a team must pass to one of two outside outlets before it can attack. Possession changes require the new attacking team to use an outlet first.
coaching_points: Transition quickly after winning the puck.
Use give-and-go movement after passing to an outlet.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and angle play outside.

title: 3 on 2 Keep Away Game
description: Two 3-on-2 keep-away areas are set up around the faceoff circles. One group plays at a time while attackers maintain possession and defenders work to block and deflect passes.
coaching_points: Offense keeps sticks available and uses flat, crisp passes.
Use deception instead of forcing passes through pressure.
Defenders keep sticks on the ice and recover to the middle.

title: 4 vs 2 Transition Game
description: Continuous 4-on-2 possession game. When the defenders win the puck, two teammates jump in as outlets and the previous attackers rotate so the possession immediately flips.
coaching_points: Blue-line players stay alert for instant transitions.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and identify outlets quickly.
Attackers move without the puck to create support.

title: Weak Side Attack
description: Two-part rush drill. The first puck creates a 2-on-1; a second puck then activates a third forward who attacks the weak side while teammates join to create a 3-on-2.
coaching_points: Second puck carrier attacks the weak side with patience.
Scan for late support before forcing the play.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and communicate through the transition.

title: Puck In Skates Skill Builder
category: Puck Control / Puck Handling / Skill Development
description: Players work the puck into their skates while moving, then use either skate to redirect it cleanly back to the stick. The drill builds comfort handling pucks that arrive in the feet and teaches quick recovery without losing skating rhythm.
coaching_points: Use both the front and back skate to control the puck.
Move the puck from the feet back to the stick quickly and cleanly.
Keep skating through the touch instead of stopping to find the puck.

title: Layered 1 v 1's
description: A forward attacks through two separate defensive layers. The first defender can pressure only in the upper zone and the second defender activates in the lower zone, forcing the puck carrier to solve two consecutive 1-on-1 problems in tight space.
coaching_points: Forward scans each defender's body and stick position before attacking.
Defenders angle and close space without leaving their assigned layer.
Encourage quick, creative puck and skating decisions between the two layers.

title: Start & Stop Loose Puck Battle
description: Two players explode from the hash marks to the blue line, stop, then race back to a loose puck near the top of the circle. The player who wins possession attacks the net while the other immediately defends.
coaching_points: Use explosive starts and complete stops to win the race.
Puck winner protects with body position before attacking the net.
Defender closes quickly with stick-on-puck and good body position.

title: Figure 8 Puck Protection Drill
description: The puck carrier works a figure-eight around two stationary defenders before attacking the net for a quick shot. The format teaches body positioning, puck placement and tight turns while pressure can be increased as players improve.
coaching_points: Use hips, arms and legs to keep the body between the defender and puck.
Keep the puck outside and away from pressure.
Use tight, powerful turns to stay strong on the puck and build speed.

title: Corner Boards 1 V 1 Loose Puck Battle
description: Two players battle for a loose puck along the corner boards. The player who wins possession attacks the net while the other defends; the format can progress from 1-on-1 to 2-on-2.
coaching_points: Arrive low and balanced to establish body position.
Offense protects the puck with the body and uses tight turns to create space.
Defense keeps the stick on the ice and separates the player from the puck.

title: 1 v 1 Puck Battle to 2 v 2
description: The drill begins with a 1-on-1 race and battle for possession. The winner moves the puck to a teammate at the top of the circle, activating a 2-on-2 while the net-front defender becomes live.
coaching_points: Create contact and establish position before trying to possess the loose puck.
Puck winner finds the support player quickly to activate the 2-on-2.
Transition immediately from the initial battle into offensive or defensive responsibility.

title: Simple Passing & Shooting Drill
description: A player skates around a cone, receives a pass and shoots, then continues around a second cone for another pass from the opposite side and a second shot. The setup can be reduced for station work.
coaching_points: Keep the stick on the ice and call for the pass.
Receive in a shooting-ready position and release quickly.
Attack rebounds after the second shot when a goalie is in net.

title: Up and Back Progression Drill
description: A continuous full-ice transition progression. Part one begins as a 1-on-1 and becomes a 2-on-2 on the next whistle; the larger progression advances from a 2-on-1 into a 3-on-3.
coaching_points: Communicate through every transition.
Stop and rejoin the play immediately on the next whistle.
Recover hard through the middle and identify new assignments quickly.

title: Rondo Circle Passing Progression
description: Six to eight players work through a circle passing progression that builds from one puck to two pucks, follow-your-pass movement, and one- or two-defender keep-away. An advanced variation transitions a turnover into a 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Pass with hands away from the body and present the stick as a clear target.
Keep the head up when multiple pucks and players are moving.
Use hands, eyes and body language to disguise passing intentions.

title: Give and Go Shooting Station
description: A player works two consecutive give-and-go passes with stationary support players, then finishes with a quick-release shot. Players rotate through the shooter and support positions after each repetition.
coaching_points: Keep the stick on the ice as a passing target.
Move immediately after making each pass.
Use one-touch passes and a quick release whenever execution allows.

title: Battery Quick Release Shooting Series
description: Four-part quick-release shooting series built around receiving a pass and shooting without extra stickhandles. The passer and shooting lane change through center and both wings so players solve different catch-and-release angles.
coaching_points: Keep the stick on the ice so the passer sees the target.
Receive the puck directly into the shooting box.
Use the bottom hand to load the stick and release immediately after the pass.

title: Howie's Warm Up Skating Evaluation Drill
description: Players move through a full-ice skating pattern featuring crossovers around circles, stops, side-steps across blue and red lines, and repeated accelerations. The drill can also be performed backward for defensemen.
coaching_points: Complete every stop before accelerating into the next segment.
Stay low and controlled through crossovers and lateral steps.
Use the pattern to evaluate edge control, balance and acceleration on both sides.

title: Pop Warm Up Drill
description: Defensemen collect three pucks from the neutral-zone circle. The first two are passed to forwards on opposite sides for rush shots; the third is used by the defenseman for an escape and a shot while the forwards can remain at the net for tips and screens.
coaching_points: Communicate and present the stick as a target.
Keep the head up through passes, escapes and rush skating.
Shoot in stride and use the two forwards around the net for traffic and tips.

title: Puck Protection - Surround Puck
description: Two players start on opposite sides of a circle with the puck placed slightly closer to the designated protector. On the whistle they battle; the protector uses body position to surround the puck and keep possession inside the circle.
coaching_points: Take away the defender's stick before reaching for the puck.
Use the body to surround and shield possession.
Stay low and strong on the edges while keeping the puck inside the circle.

title: 3 v 2 Puck Protection Game
description: Three attackers play against two defenders on one half of the zone. If the defenders win possession they rim the puck to a weak-side teammate, who activates with the other two players to become the next three-player offensive group.
coaching_points: Offense maintains close triangle support and attacks quickly after winning possession.
The high forward supports low battles to create a numbers advantage.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes, force play outside and move the puck quickly to the weak-side outlet.

title: Corner Tires - Small Area Game
description: Players compete in a confined area and score by hitting one of two tires on the opponent's side. The game can be played 1-on-1, 2-on-2 or 3-on-3 and forces players to protect the puck while identifying open space.
coaching_points: Protect the puck and keep the head up.
Move to open space when you do not have the puck.
Use verbal and non-verbal communication to create outlets.

title: Offense to Defense 2 on 2
description: Two attackers play 2-on-2 against two defenders in a small area. When the defenders gain possession they must make a clean tape-to-tape pass to the next offensive group; the previous attackers then become the defenders, making the game continuous.
coaching_points: Attackers try to isolate one defender and create a 2-on-1 inside the 2-on-2.
Defenders communicate, stay inside and control the puck before exiting.
Both sides protect possession until a clean play is available.

title: 7 Pass 2 vs. 1 Small Area Game
description: Two offensive players work against one defender inside a tight neutral-zone box. The offense tries to complete seven consecutive passes while the defender disrupts possession; a goalie variation allows the attackers to go to the net after the seventh pass.
coaching_points: Pass and move instead of passing and watching.
Off-puck player constantly presents a good target.
Defender uses active sticks, hard stops and straight-line pressure.

title: Swiss 4 vs. 2 Scoring Game
description: Four attackers play against two defenders in two connected 2-on-1 spaces. Attackers can pass across the full group while defenders remain responsible for their assigned half, creating repeated scoring and deception decisions under pressure.
coaching_points: Scan before receiving and know the next option.
Use deception to create passing or shooting lanes.
Attack the net when a clear shooting opportunity appears.
Defenders use body and stick position to remove cross-ice options.

title: Chute Angling 1 V 1
description: The puck is banked or shot toward the blue line for an offensive player to retrieve while a second player closes as the defender. After retrieval, the forward attacks the net and the defender works to angle the puck carrier outside and win possession.
coaching_points: Defender matches speed, keeps the stick on the ice and angles toward the boards.
Puck carrier uses deception before retrieval and keeps the feet moving.
Both players keep the head up and react to body position rather than fakes.

title: World Passing & Stickhandling Warm-Up
description: Four to six players form around a faceoff circle while two players work inside with pucks. The inside players use creative stickhandling, edgework, escapes and deception, then pass to an outside player who rotates into the circle.
coaching_points: Keep the head up while handling inside the circle.
Use edges, escapes and deception instead of repeating one move.
Outside players keep sticks ready as clear passing targets.

title: Blueline Agility Reps
description: Forwards retrieve pucks from the corner or goalie, pass to the point, then move to the net while a defenseman walks the blue line and gets a shot through traffic. The sequence gives defenders repeated lateral blue-line footwork and forwards repeated retrieval-to-point habits.
coaching_points: Forwards shoulder-check before retrieval and then create a screen or tip at the net.
Defenseman moves laterally as soon as the puck arrives to create a new shooting lane.
Get the point shot through sticks quickly instead of overhandling.

title: Neutral Zone Support 2 on 1
description: Both forwards sprint to the blue line, work tight control turns back around cones, then attack together after one player collects a puck. The defenseman performs a backward-forward transition pattern before defending the 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Second forward times support so the puck carrier has both a direct and wall-chip option.
Defenseman controls the gap through the transition and protects the middle.
Forwards attack with speed and maintain useful spacing.

title: 3 v 3 Mystery Player Game
description: Before each rep, each three-player team secretly sets an order for who must take the first, second and third shots. The opposing team does not know the order, creating a 3-on-3 problem-solving game that rewards communication, puck movement and retrievals.
coaching_points: Create time and space for the designated shooter instead of forcing the puck.
After each shot, win the retrieval and reorganize for the next shooter.
Talk between reps about what created or removed scoring space.

title: 2 vs 2 Game (With 1 Goalie & Tire Nets)
category: 2 vs 2 / One Goalie / Small Area Game
description: Cross-ice game built for practices with one goalie. One team attacks the goalie while the other team scores by hitting tire targets at the opposite end. Teams rotate so everyone gets reps attacking both types of targets.
coaching_points: Play with the head up and communicate.
Move after passing to create give-and-go options.
Use different target numbers or rink sizes to adjust difficulty.

title: 3 vs. 3 Split Zone Game
description: The zone is divided in half for a 3-on-3 with one goalie. Offense works to score while defense must gain possession, complete a pass and exit its half of the zone to earn a point.
coaching_points: Offense protects possession and uses the boards to create time and space.
Off-puck players stay available as outlets.
Defenders communicate, keep sticks in lanes and make a clean pass before exiting.

title: Shooting Off The Pass - Corners
description: A passer jumps from the net-front area into the corner to receive a puck from the half wall. The original puck carrier then jumps to open space toward the net, receives the return pass and releases the shot immediately.
coaching_points: Use verbal and non-verbal communication before the pass.
Both players jump to open space instead of standing still.
Shoot off the return pass with as little settling time as possible.

title: 5 V 5 to 5 V 3 Face-off Game On The Circle
description: A half-zone game begins with a 5-on-5 faceoff. Once possession is clear, the losing team removes two players, creating a 5-on-3 advantage for the faceoff winner while both teams continue trying to score.
coaching_points: Centers get low and strong on the stick during the faceoff.
Wingers react immediately to support loose-puck possession.
The five-player group moves the puck quickly while the three defenders keep sticks in lanes.

title: Angle Through The Dot 1 V 1
description: The defender passes to an attacker moving down the wall, then skates through a narrow obstacle gate before angling into the 1-on-1. The puck carrier attacks with speed and works to protect the puck while driving through the check.
coaching_points: Defender matches speed, steers with the stick and closes through the hands.
Puck carrier keeps feet moving and protects the puck on the outside.
Both players work to stay balanced through contact and direction changes.
